_comment: Raw TCP service contract, governed by ADR-0102 (feature 142).
A user-facing raw TCP listener runs IN-PROCESS, folded into each runtime's
existing accept/event loop. The app registers callbacks (on_connect, on_data,
on_close, optional on_line), frames the raw byte stream itself (binary/length/
CRC - the car-tracker case), identifies a connection by an app id (the IMEI),
and pushes server->device commands through a name-keyed registry (send_to /
connection / broadcast). The framework owns the socket hard-parts: lifecycle,
max_connections refusal, an idle reaper (default OFF for long-lived device
STATE: every invariant below is OWED - the rule and its executable cases are
declared, but no suite proves them yet (no framework code exists; planning
only). Each invariant therefore carries NO 'suites' block. When the Python
reference and the ports land, add the per-language 'suites' map (the intended
filenames are listed under 'planned_suites' for each), which flips the
invariant from owed to proven and makes scripts/audit-contract-fixtures.py
check that each named case exists in all four suites. NO MOCKS: every case
runs a REAL client socket against a REAL in-process listener, and each must be
proven able to FAIL by mutation before it counts.
Python is the reference (ADR-0004). Build order: python -> php -> ruby -> node.

invariants.rule: tcp_service(port) opens a listener folded into the running framework's existing accept/event loop (not a second blocking loop, not a separate daemon by default); a real client that connects fires on_connect(conn) while the HTTP server keeps serving.
invariants.why: D1: the whole value is one process serving both the device gateway and its HTTP dashboard. A second blocking loop or a separate daemon would defeat the shared-process reuse of config/logging/ORM/queue.

cases.name: client connects and on_connect fires in the server process
cases.given: a Tina4 app serving HTTP with a tcp_service registered on a free port
cases.when: a real TCP client opens a socket to that port
cases.then: on_connect(conn) is invoked once in the same process and an HTTP request to the app still succeeds concurrently

invariants.rule: on_data(conn, bytes) delivers the raw bytes exactly as received (never newline-split, never decoded); on_line(conn, line) delivers one newline-delimited line with the terminator stripped; on_close(conn) fires exactly once when the peer or server closes.
invariants.why: D2/D3: tracker frames are binary/length/CRC, so the app must see raw bytes and frame them itself; on_line is a text convenience only. Per-connection coroutine handlers were rejected (do not port to Node/PHP).

cases.name: on_data delivers raw bytes not split on newlines
cases.given: a connection with an on_data handler recording every buffer it receives
cases.when: the client sends bytes containing embedded 0x0A and a trailing partial frame
cases.then: the handler sees the raw bytes (no split, no decode), and the app's own buffering reassembles frames

cases.name: on_line splits a newline-delimited stream
cases.given: a connection with an on_line handler
cases.when: the client sends 'a\nb\nc' with no trailing newline
cases.then: on_line fires for 'a' and 'b' (terminator stripped) and 'c' stays buffered until its newline arrives

cases.name: on_close fires once when the peer closes
cases.then: on_close(conn) is invoked exactly once and the connection is removed from the registry

invariants.rule: The app can write a reply to an inbound packet with conn.send(bytes); the exact bytes are received by that client socket in order.
invariants.why: D5: ACK-per-packet is the tracker norm (the server replies to each location packet). conn.send must put raw bytes on that specific socket.

cases.name: a binary frame round-trips and is ACKed
cases.given: an on_data handler that replies with a fixed ACK byte sequence
cases.when: the client sends a binary login/location frame
cases.then: the client reads back the exact ACK bytes, in order, on the same socket

invariants.rule: conn.identify(app_id) registers the live connection under the app id; tcp(name).send_to(app_id, bytes) writes to exactly that device's socket; tcp(name).broadcast(bytes) writes to all; send_to to an unknown or closed id is a no-op return, never a raise; a second connection identifying with the same id supersedes the first in the registry.
invariants.why: D4: server->device commands ('set interval', 'cut fuel') are addressed by IMEI from an HTTP route. Without the registry the feature can only ingest.

cases.name: identify registers and send_to reaches that socket
cases.given: a connection that calls conn.identify('imeiA') from its login handler
cases.then: the cmd bytes are received by that same client socket

cases.name: send_to is isolated to the addressed device
cases.then: the 'imeiA' socket receives cmd and the 'imeiB' socket receives nothing

cases.name: send_to to an unknown id is a no-op not a raise
cases.then: the call returns falsey/None without raising and no bytes are sent

cases.name: broadcast reaches every live connection
cases.then: all three client sockets receive msg

cases.name: re-identify with the same id supersedes the first
cases.then: send_to('imeiA') reaches connection two (the live one), matching a device that reconnected

invariants.rule: Every connection exposes send(bytes), close(), remote_addr (the raw socket peer, never a forwarded header), id (the registry id, null until identified), identify(app_id), and context (a per-connection mutable state bag).
invariants.why: D5: a uniform connection object across all four is what makes the primitive portable; context holds the IMEI, auth state and parse buffer.

cases.name: remote_addr is the raw socket peer
cases.given: a client connecting from a known local address
cases.then: it is the raw TCP peer address, not any forwarded/proxy header value

cases.name: context persists across on_data calls for one connection
cases.given: a handler that accumulates a parse buffer in conn.context
cases.when: the client sends a frame across two separate writes
cases.then: the second on_data sees the buffer the first left in conn.context, and a different connection has its own

cases.name: close() ends the connection and fires on_close
cases.then: the client socket is closed, on_close fires once, and the registry entry is removed

invariants.rule: With max_connections=N set, the (N+1)th connection is refused or immediately closed, never queued unbounded.
invariants.why: A device fleet must not be able to exhaust server memory/fds; the limit is a hard refusal, not an unbounded accept backlog.

cases.name: the N+1th connection is refused
cases.given: a tcp_service with max_connections=2 and two live connections
cases.when: a third client attempts to connect
cases.then: the third connection is refused or closed promptly and the two existing connections are unaffected

invariants.rule: idle_timeout defaults to 0 (OFF): a silent connection stays open indefinitely. With idle_timeout>0 a connection with no activity for that many seconds is closed and on_close fires.
invariants.why: D1 consumer shape: tracker sockets are deliberately long-lived and mostly idle between location packets, so the reaper must default OFF or it would kill healthy devices.

cases.name: idle_timeout=0 keeps a silent connection open
cases.given: a tcp_service with idle_timeout=0 and a connected client sending nothing
cases.when: a span longer than any default reap interval passes
cases.then: the connection is still open and on_close has not fired

cases.name: idle_timeout>0 reaps a silent connection
cases.given: a tcp_service with a short idle_timeout and a connected client sending nothing
cases.when: the timeout elapses with no activity
cases.then: the connection is closed and on_close fires; a connection that kept sending is not reaped

invariants.rule: On SIGTERM/SIGINT the TCP listener drains alongside the HTTP server within the shutdown deadline: live connections are closed cleanly and the HTTP server keeps serving until the deadline.
invariants.why: Parity with the graceful-shutdown contract (feature 025); a rolling deploy must not strand device connections or hang the grace period.

cases.name: live TCP connections close cleanly on SIGTERM
cases.given: a running app with an HTTP server and a tcp_service with a live connection
cases.then: the live connection is closed within the shutdown deadline and the process exits 0

invariants.rule: A slow or stalled reader does not grow server memory without bound: outbound writes queue up to a bounded backlog and a client past the backlog limit is dropped rather than buffered indefinitely.
invariants.why: D-security: an unbounded per-connection write buffer is a memory-exhaustion DoS; mirrors the WebSocket TINA4_WS_MAX_BACKLOG posture.

cases.name: a stalled reader is bounded, not buffered without limit
cases.given: a connection whose client never reads while the server sends large volumes
cases.when: the queued bytes exceed the backlog limit
cases.then: server memory stays bounded and the stalled client is dropped, while other connections keep serving

invariants.rule: Under a multi-worker HTTP deployment the TCP listener binds in exactly ONE owner (the primary worker); SO_REUSEPORT is off by default, so N workers do not each bind the port.
invariants.why: D1 consequence (Python/PHP): N processes each binding the port is the first thing that breaks under a process manager; one owner avoids split device state and duplicate accepts.

cases.name: only one worker binds the TCP port
cases.given: the HTTP side configured with N>1 workers and a tcp_service registered
cases.then: exactly one worker binds and accepts on the TCP port; the others do not bind it, and no bind error is raised
